title: A. Pelissier to Pierre Jeannin, Burgos, 13 September 1592 (BnF fr. 3982 no. 22)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's key image and web search: no published decipherment of no. 22.
377 cipher runs transcribed sign by sign (pass 1, agents).
Re-deriving the key by letter-frequency hill-climbing on the noisy transcription collapsed to an all-e attractor.
Tomokiyo's key applied with a quadgram beam search over each sign's candidate letters; glosses agree.
Calibration: nos. 45/46 aligned sign by sign with the f. 115 clear text (1,764 signs), splitting merged glyph families.
Open-letter diagnostic decode showed the merged tokens directly, matching the calibration.
Pass 3 re-read all nine pages with the split tokens: 94% of cipher words.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's key for Pelissier's letters (cryptiana league.htm, rebuilt from nos. 45/46 and their f. 115 decipherment) was applied to a sign-by-sign transcription of no. 22 by beam search; the sign shapes were calibrated by aligning nos. 45/46 with f. 115, and the scattered interlinear glosses agree.
outcome.fraction_read_source: READING.md: words inside deciphered {..} stretches (plaintext words, not cipher signs): 3,936 tokens, 256 [?] gaps counted unread = 0.935; the 158 (?) doubtful words counted read (0.89 if unread)
outcome.notes: Read in part under the read bar: 0.93 of plaintext words measured (below 0.95); about 250 words of no. 22 stay unread.

gaps.item: code group 310 (f. 50r, probably Savoy), 441 (f. 49v, probably France) and the confessor's name on f. 50r

gaps.detail: single hard glyphs after the calibrated high-zoom re-read (pass 3), listed per page in reading_<folio>.md

gaps.item: holes in the paper, f. 50r C13
gaps.detail: paper lost; no other copy of no. 22

prior.where: Contemporary interlinear glosses on the letter; key published by Tomokiyo (cryptiana league.htm); no published decipherment of no. 22

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue.
